proof_nl:
Work in the field of rational functions in q, so that all displayed divisions are legitimate formal operations. Since 0 <= a <= b and a + b <= n, the number r := n - a - b is a nonnegative integer, and
n - a = r + b,    n - b = r + a.
Hence all q-Pochhammer symbols that appear below have nonnegative indices.

By the stated definition of the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient,
([n choose b]_q)/([n choose a]_q)
= ((q;q)_n / ((q;q)_b (q;q)_{n-b})) / ((q;q)_n / ((q;q)_a (q;q)_{n-a}))
= ((q;q)_a (q;q)_{n-a}) / ((q;q)_b (q;q)_{n-b})
= ((q;q)_a (q;q)_{r+b}) / ((q;q)_b (q;q)_{r+a}).

Now use the definition (q;q)_m = product_{j=1}^m (1 - q^j) together with the empty-product convention. Because a <= b,
(q;q)_b = (product_{j=1}^a (1 - q^j)) (product_{j=a+1}^b (1 - q^j))
= (q;q)_a * product_{i=a+1}^b (1 - q^i).
Similarly,
(q;q)_{r+b} = (product_{j=1}^{r+a} (1 - q^j)) (product_{j=r+a+1}^{r+b} (1 - q^j))
= (q;q)_{r+a} * product_{j=r+a+1}^{r+b} (1 - q^j).
Reindex the last product by j = r + i. As i runs from a+1 to b, j runs from r+a+1 to r+b, so
product_{j=r+a+1}^{r+b} (1 - q^j) = product_{i=a+1}^b (1 - q^(r+i)).
Therefore,
(q;q)_{r+b} = (q;q)_{r+a} * product_{i=a+1}^b (1 - q^(r+i)).

Substituting these two factorizations into the earlier expression gives
([n choose b]_q)/([n choose a]_q)
= ((q;q)_a (q;q)_{r+a} * product_{i=a+1}^b (1 - q^(r+i))) / (((q;q)_a * product_{i=a+1}^b (1 - q^i)) (q;q)_{r+a})
= (product_{i=a+1}^b (1 - q^(r+i))) / (product_{i=a+1}^b (1 - q^i))
= product_{i=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)).

If a = b, each product from i = a+1 to b is empty, hence equal to 1, and the same computation yields 1 on both sides. Thus the claimed identity holds for all integers n, a, b with 0 <= a <= b and a + b <= n.
solver_summary: Substitute the definition of the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient, use n-a = r+b and n-b = r+a, factor (q;q)_b at level a and (q;q)_{r+b} at level r+a, then cancel the common q-Pochhammer factors. The remaining quotient is exactly product_{i=a+1}^b ((1-q^(r+i))/(1-q^i)).

The hypotheses 0 <= a <= b and a+b <= n are used exactly to ensure all q-Pochhammer indices are nonnegative and the interval products are well-formed. No forbidden or undeclared dependencies are used.
